Vendor learning path

SAP S/4HANA Materials Management and adjacent products

SAP S/4HANA is an ERP. Materials Management (MM) is its purchasing and inventory heart: requisitions, POs, goods receipts and invoice verification. Around it sit SAP Ariba (source-to-pay on the business network), SAP EWM (warehouse), SAP TM (transport) and SAP IBP (planning).

ERPS2PWMSTMSPlanning

Learning path

Foundations

Beginner / BA
  • What an ERP is and why MM sits at its centre
  • Organisational structure: company code, plant, storage location, purchasing organisation
  • Master data: material, Business Partner, info record, source list
  • Walk the P2P chain: PR → PO → GR → invoice → payment

Exercise. Trace one PO from requisition to payment and name the document created at each step.

Functional

Consultant
  • Document types, item categories (standard, consignment, subcontracting, service) and account assignment
  • Release strategy vs flexible workflow for approvals
  • Pricing: condition records, info records, contracts, scheduling agreements
  • Inventory management: movement types, stock types (unrestricted, quality, blocked)
  • Logistics invoice verification: GR-based IV, tolerance keys, duplicate check, blocked invoices
  • MRP basics: reorder point planning vs MRP Live

Exercise. Configure a scenario: 3-way match with 2% quantity tolerance and price variance block; test the 100/95/100 case.

Technical

Developer / Data
  • Released APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub: purchase order, supplier invoice, goods movement
  • IDoc basics: ORDERS05, DESADV, INVOIC02 and partner profiles
  • Business events and SAP Event Mesh
  • Clean-core extensibility: key user extensions, side-by-side apps on SAP BTP
  • Data: EKKO/EKPO (PO), MSEG/MATDOC (goods movements), RBKP/RSEG (invoices) for analytics

Exercise. Build a small service that consumes PurchaseOrder events and posts a goods receipt via API, idempotent on the WMS transaction id.

Architecture

Architect
  • Clean core and upgrade-safe integration
  • Where Ariba vs S/4HANA owns sourcing, PO and invoice
  • EWM embedded vs decentralised
  • Event-driven integration with non-SAP OMS/WMS
  • Master data governance for Business Partner and material

Exercise. Design the target landscape for a retailer using S/4HANA + Manhattan OMS/WMS + Coupa for indirect spend.

Same concept, SAP vocabulary

Generic termSAP
SupplierBusiness Partner (supplier role); "vendor" in older ECC
Purchase requisitionPurchase requisition (ME51N)
Purchase orderPurchase order (ME21N)
Price agreementPurchasing info record · contract (outline agreement)
Goods receiptGoods receipt, movement type 101 (MIGO)
Invoice matchingLogistics invoice verification (MIRO)
Price/qty toleranceTolerance keys (e.g. PP price variance, DQ quantity)
Held invoiceBlocked for payment (release via MRBR)
Liability for received goodsGR/IR clearing account
Payment runAutomatic payment program (F110)
OrganisationCompany code · plant · storage location · purchasing org

Use cases

Stock replenishment for a retail DC with GST

An Indian retailer replenishes its Hoskote DC from 3 suppliers.

MRP or reorder-point planning creates PRs; source list and info records assign supplier and price; POs go out via EDI; WMS confirms receipts that post as 101 goods movements; MIRO matches invoices with GST tax codes; F110 pays on due date.

KPIs: First-pass match rate · PO-to-receipt lead time · stockouts

Quality-controlled inbound for regulated goods

Pharma or food items must pass inspection before stock is usable.

GR posts into quality inspection stock; an inspection lot is created; the usage decision moves stock to unrestricted. Invoice verification relies on accepted quantities, effectively a 4-way match.

KPIs: Inspection cycle time · blocked invoice value

Integration surface

OData/REST APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub (e.g. API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV, API_SUPPLIERINVOICE_PROCESS_SRV), IDocs (ORDERS05, INVOIC02, DESADV), business events (e.g. PurchaseOrder.Created) via SAP Event Mesh / Integration Suite, SAP Business Network for supplier B2B.

Product names and modules evolve. Verify against current SAP documentation.
